reason: The hypothesis directly applies the proven 'microstructure inversion' strategy from P2/P9 (discrete B2 in a continuous BCC matrix) to a new alloy, NbZrTiHfMo, and adds a new mechanistic rationale—that Mo partitioning into B2 precipitates reduces the electronegativity difference in the matrix to enhance dislocation mobility. This mechanism is not stated in any passage and links the microstructural change to a specific electronic-level cause for improved ductility, going beyond a simple transfer of a known recipe.
copied_elements: two-step heat treatment (solutionizing + aging) to invert microstructure from P9
microstructure inversion from continuous B2 + discrete BCC to continuous BCC + discrete B2 from P2, P4
precipitation strengthening from B2 precipitates from P2
enhanced ductility while retaining high strength from P2, P10
falsification test design (control vs. treated, TEM, compression) is standard practice
